title: Diagnostic: Why @State Exists

docs.title: Managing model data in your app

hints: `body` can't mutate the view struct's own stored properties.
Declare `var count = 0` without a property wrapper and increment it in a button action.
jsBridge: A SwiftUI view is a struct, and `body` isn't `mutating`, so `count += 1` can't compile. `@State` moves the storage outside the struct, which is SwiftUI's `useState`. Like React, the view is recreated often and state must live elsewhere.

compass.q: Why can't a React component keep state in a local variable either? How is `@State` like `useState`?
`@State` vs `@Binding` vs `@Observable` model: who owns the data in each?
Why must `@State` be `private` by convention? What happens if a parent passes an initial value?
Initialising `@State` from a parameter only takes effect once. Why, and what's the fix (`.onChange`, `id`)?
